name: Shift4 Payments

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Integrated payments plus software for hospitality, restaurants, stadiums and luxury retail, and since the July 2025 Global Blue deal, tax-free shopping refunds for travellers.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: Q3 gross revenue $1,319M: payments-based $1,073M, tax-free shopping $139M, subscription and other $107M (-10% y/y per letter). Payments-based GRLNF $402M of $648M total.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Many merchants across restaurants, hotels, venues, luxury brands; Kahala Brands is now largest restaurant customer. No single customer above 10% disclosed in what was read (not exhaustively checked).

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: 67% of 6,300 staff are outside the US across 59 countries; worldwide ex-Americas payments GRLNF +44% YTD; euro notes $1,266M; FX and travel disruption named as headwinds.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Takes a spread (Blended Spread 64 bps vs ~60 bps target) on card volume ($61B in Q3, +11%) plus software and tax-refund fees; mostly recurring per-transaction, paid as volume flows.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Capex $63-74M a quarter (equipment, software); Adj EBITDA margin 48% on GRLNF (50% a year ago); FY guide cut: GRLNF ~4% and Adj EBITDA ~6% below the original 2026 plan; volume guide upper end trimmed to $240-250B.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Inputs: Visa/Mastercard network fees ($671M in Q3, passed to merchants and netted out in GRLNF); one vendor processes North American merchant activity and a sponsor bank is needed (single points of failure); funding via term loan and notes. Pass-through: network fees yes; interest costs no ($78M Q3 vs $61M a year ago). Signal tags: rates (floating term loan $1,990M at 6.35%), dollar and travel (tax-free shopping, euro debt), consumer_spending_nominal (percent-of-sale revenue), regulation (interchange).

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Claims #1 in US hospitality and sports/entertainment, #2 in US restaurants, #1 in luxury tax-free retail; 'unmatched software integration library'. Doing differently now: Shift4 One unified platform live in 15 countries, trading single-product revenue for payments revenue.

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: A business-to-business brand; consumers see it at checkout but do not choose it. Not an everyday household name. Marketing spend not separately checked.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Competes with Chase Paymentech, Elavon, Fiserv, Global Payments, Adyen, Toast, Square, Lightspeed. Company says it is gaining share; volume +11% and payments GRLNF +18% in Q3 suggest so, but rivals' volume not compared here.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Payments GRLNF +23% YTD vs low-20s target; international in 15 countries; pending $143M cash Paramount Commerce deal (up to $317M); Global Blue synergies ~$50M exiting 2026 toward $70M by 2027.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: LTM GAAP free cash flow about $371M (156+66-9+158) vs adjusted $470M guide (42% of Adj EBITDA); net debt about $4.3B = 3.8x LTM Adj EBITDA of $1,132M; repurchased 5.5M shares in H1 and 4.2M in Q3; insiders and employees hold over 40% per CEO letter; Rook (founder) 28.4% of Class A. Pay rewards Adj EBITDA (PvP table).

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Not losing relevance: volume 2.9x Q3 2022. But travel disruption and weak same-store sales hit Q4 harder; subscription revenue -10% in Q3; growth leans on acquisitions; founder (25% of votes) now serves as NASA Administrator and resigned as Executive Chairman Dec 2025.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: Clean: no 4.01/4.02, no NT filings, no CORRESP/UPLOAD in 3 years, clean ICFR opinion (PCAOB ID 238), Global Blue valuation is the critical audit matter. Flags: Q3 Adj EBITDA $310M vs EBITDA $261M (+19%); non-GAAP EPS $1.49 vs GAAP $0.37; Adj FCF adds back $151M YTD; chief accounting officer left Apr 2026 (interim replacement).

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Overheat: nominal volume helps, but a strong dollar and rising rates hurt (floating debt, tourists). Slowdown: travel and discretionary dining/stadium spend soften first and 3.8x leverage bites. Stagflation: real spend falls, debt costs rise. Boom is best.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Exposed to card network rules, interchange/Credit Card Competition Act, EU/UK payment rules, tax-free shopping regimes in 40+ countries; pending Paramount close needs routine approvals in Q4 2026. No specific adverse docket found.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: At $43.58 (about 88M shares incl. preferred, equity ~$3.8B, EV ~$8.3B), reverse DCF: LTM GAAP FCF $371M must shrink ~2% a year (or $290M after stock comp must grow only ~1.5%) to justify price; own OCF grew 275M (2022) to 634M (2025). EV/Adj EBITDA ~7.4x, ~8.5x non-GAAP EPS guide $5.05-5.15. Own 5-year range and peer multiples not pulled.

status_reason: Organic growth is real (9-10%) and the price implies shrinking cash flow, but 3.8x net leverage, a guidance cut and large non-GAAP add-backs leave the cushion unproven in a Slowdown turn.
the_mistake: Market treats it as a debt-funded roll-up whose cash flow will shrink; filings show 9% organic growth, payments revenue +18%, record adjusted free cash flow, and the 2027 convertible ($633M) already covered by $1.24B cash and a new term loan.
what_makes_market_notice: Q4 2026 results (around Feb 2027) showing synergies near $50M and free cash flow at the $465-475M guide; Paramount close in Q4 2026; reduced travel disruption.

feedback.fact: CEO letter: travel disruption (worse in Q4), currency fluctuation, inflation and weaker same-store sales are headwinds; volume guide trimmed to $240-250B. Confirms dollar and soft real-spend reads.
